author: goldturtle
body:
@marcfeuermann @pgaudet: submitted with the PAINT issue template's fields. The posting account cannot set labels, so please add `PAINT annotation`.

* **PTHR ID & PTN node:** PTHR24419; PTN008405164 (gain of positive regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction, GO:0043123)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):** UniProtKB:Q9Y616 IRAK3 (interleukin 1 receptor associated kinase 3)

* **Type of Issue:** Other: possible erroneous propagation from paralogs, but IRAK3's own opposing annotation (and the same IMP on IRAK1 and IRAK2) looks mis-curated, so please review before acting.

*How this draft was made:* an automated screen compared every PAN-GO (IBA) annotation of human genes (release 2025-10-12_2.0.5, PANTHER 19) with the genes' experimental annotations in GO release 2025-10-10. Flagged annotations were then judged by evidence-cited reasoning (Claude subagents, citing only a curated evidence pack). The statements below were checked against the GO, PAN-GO and PANTHER data, and the papers behind the key annotations were read. Please treat it as a candidate for curator review.


*Also dropped since v1: in v1, IRAK3 inherited negative regulation of MAP kinase activity, of tumor necrosis factor production and of interleukin-12 production from its own subclade PTN002815516, together with positive regulation of NF-kappaB transcription factor activity. It inherits none of these now, so like BCL2 and FMR1 it has lost its negative-regulation annotations.*

**Inherited:** IRAK3 `involved_in` *positive regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction* ([GO:0043123](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0043123))

- **Gain:** PTN008405164 (speciation, Craniata-Tunicata; human genes below: IRAK1, IRAK2, IRAK3, IRAK4), dated 2024-07-26.
- **Evidence genes (2):** IRAK1 (HUMAN), IRAK4 (HUMAN).
- **Relation to IRAK3:** paralogs: IRAK1 (HUMAN), IRAK4 (HUMAN).
- **Other human genes inheriting it:** IRAK1, IRAK2, IRAK4.
- **Losses of this term in the family:** none.
- **v1 (paper release):** not annotated.

**IRAK3's own experimental annotations** (GO release 2025-10-10) against *positive regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction*: 1 opposing, 0 supporting:

- *negative regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction* ([GO:0043124](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0043124)): [PMID:10383454](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10383454/) (IMP)

**Literature (Textpresso, all species corpora):** 8 sentences mention IRAK3 together with *canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction*. By cue words, 3 describe the opposite of the inherited direction and 1 agree.

> Discussion IRAK-M is an endogenous negative regulator of TLR signaling that prevents uncontrolled inflammation after tissue injury in multiple diseases. **IRAK-M prevents dissociation of IRAK-1 and IRAK-4 from MyD88 and inhibits formation of IRAK-TRAF6 complexes and subsequent IκB degradation and NF-κB nuclear translocation.** Nevertheless, its role in the cerebrovascular disorders is unclear.

— Lyu C, Zhang Y, Gu M, Huang Y, Liu G, Wang C et al. (2018). IRAK-M Deficiency Exacerbates Ischemic Neurovascular Injuries in Experimental Stroke Mice. *Frontiers in cellular neuroscience*. [PMID:30622459](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30622459/).


> Next, the authors investigated the effects of IRAK-M deficiency on TLR signalling pathways. **TLR engagement on IRAK-M -/-macrophages led to more rapid phosphorylation of IκBα -a member of the NF-κB family -and a faster and more extensive phosphorylation of JNK, p38 and ERK1/2, which indicates that IRAK-M might negatively regulate these pathways.** Nature now show that DCs might be able to enhance the probability of productive interactions with T cells by the directed trafficking of peptide-MHC complexes along tubules that extend towards the sites of contact with T cells.

— Nature Reviews Immunology research highlights (2002). Textpresso document AGRKB:101000000830868 combines several highlights, and its record names only one of them (Alfred J, "C. elegans - an innate choice?"), which is not the source of the sentences cited here. Not in PubMed.


**Sentences counted as agreeing** (1): it does support the inherited term, in an overexpression experiment.

> In contrast, other reports indicate that IRAK-M may act as an inducing mediator in the TLR/IL-1R signaling pathway. **Notably, overexpression of IRAK-M in HEK293 cells activates NF-κB, an effect that is dependent on the IRAK-M N-terminal DD domain58.** Overexpression of IRAK-M in IRAK1 KO cells is sufficient to restore IL-1-induced NF-κB activation58, indicating that IRAK-M and IRAK1 may exert similar functions under certain stimulations.

— Nechama M, Kwon J, Wei S, Kyi AT, Welner RS, Ben-Dov IZ et al. (2018). The IL-33-PIN1-IRAK-M axis is critical for type 2 immunity in IL-33-induced allergic airway inflammation. *Nature communications*. [PMID:29686383](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29686383/).


**Reasoning** (evidence-cited; verdict *error likely*, medium confidence; cause: paralog inheritance): IRAK3 (IRAK-M) is repeatedly described in the pack as a repressor of NF-kappaB signaling, and its own IMP annotation is to negative regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signaling. The inherited positive-regulation term comes only from its paralogs IRAK1 and IRAK4 across a duplication and is a new 2024 gain. Some reports of NF-kappaB activation by overexpressed IRAK-M or a splice variant exist, but they do not justify inheriting the paralogs' positive role.

- *Against:* IRAK3 has a direct IMP annotation to negative regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction. ([PMID:10383454](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10383454/))
- *Against:* Multiple independent sources describe IRAK-M as a repressor of NF-kappaB signaling that blocks IRAK-TRAF6 complex formation, IkappaB degradation and NF-kappaB translocation, and IRAK-M-null macrophages show faster IkappaBalpha phosphorylation. (Nolan et al. 2009; Lyu et al. 2018; Li et al. 2005; Nat Rev Immunol highlights 2002; Sung et al. 2013)
- *Against:* The inherited annotation rests only on human IRAK1 and IRAK4, paralogs whose lineage meets IRAK3 at duplication node PTN002401150. (IRAK1; IRAK4; PANTHER tree)
- *Context:* The annotation is new: the gain was curated in 2024 and IRAK3 did not have it in PAN-GO v1. (PAN-GO annotation; PAN-GO v1)
- *For:* Overexpressed IRAK-M activates NF-kappaB in HEK293 cells, an Irak-m splice variant activates NF-kappaB, and IRAK-M overexpression enhanced NTHi-induced inflammation partly via NF-kappaB, so a positive role exists in some contexts. (Nechama et al. 2018; Rothschild et al. 2017; Hou et al. 2025)

*Reasoner's suggested fix:* Add a loss of positive regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction ([GO:0043123](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0043123)) at PTN002815516 (the IRAK3 subclade). *Tree check:* A loss at PTN002815516 would also cover Irak3 (MOUSE), which has its own IDA to this term (acts upstream of or within; [PMID:12054681](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12054681/); in GO release 2025-10-10 the same IDA is to positive regulation of NF-kappaB transcription factor activity).

*Note on the reasoning:* The IMP cited in the first claim ([PMID:10383454](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10383454/)) may itself be mis-curated; see the suggested change.

**Suggested change:**

- Add a loss (NOT) of *positive regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction* at **PTN000701385** (speciation, Catarrhini; human genes below: IRAK3). IRAK3's lineage meets all 2 evidence genes only at the gene duplication PTN002401150, so the function may have diverged after that duplication. It sits below Irak3 (MOUSE) rather than at PTN002815516, because Irak3 (MOUSE) is not an evidence gene but has its own IDA to this term (acts upstream of or within; [PMID:12054681](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12054681/); in GO release 2025-10-10 the same IDA is to positive regulation of NF-kappaB transcription factor activity). Mouse Irak3 also has IMP annotations ([PMID:12150927](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12150927/)) to negative regulation of cytokine production and of the innate immune response, so IRAK3 may act both ways: check before adding the loss.
- Before adding the loss, review IRAK3's only opposing experimental annotation, an IMP to negative regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction from Wesche et al. 1999 ([PMID:10383454](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10383454/)). It looks mis-curated: the paper reports IRAK-M and IRAK-2 restoring the IL-1 response in IRAK-deficient cells, a positive role, and the agreeing sentence quoted above cites the same study. The same curation (2024) gives the identical negative IMP to IRAK1 and IRAK2; IRAK1 is an evidence gene for the inherited term and has a positive IMP to it. Without these, IRAK3 has no human experimental annotation to NF-kappaB signalling in either direction. Its inhibitory role rests on mouse knockout data (Kobayashi et al. 2002, [PMID:12150927](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12150927/)) and human siRNA studies of cytokine output ([PMID:18156187](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18156187/), [PMID:15728517](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15728517/)), while mouse Irak3 also has an IDA to the inherited term. IRAK3 may act both ways, so a loss should wait for that review.

### References
- Hou H, Li J, Huang Y, Zhao Y, Gao J (2025). IRAK-M regulates NTHi-induced inflammation via JNK and NF-κB signal pathways. *Biochem Biophys Res Commun*. [PMID:40550193](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40550193/).
- Kobayashi K, Hernandez LD, Galán JE, Janeway CA, Medzhitov R, Flavell RA (2002). IRAK-M is a negative regulator of Toll-like receptor signaling. *Cell*. [PMID:12150927](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12150927/).
- Li H, Cuartas E, Cui W, Choi Y, Crawford TD, Ke HZ et al. (2005). IL-1 receptor-associated kinase M is a central regulator of osteoclast differentiation and activation. *The Journal of experimental medicine*. [PMID:15809356](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15809356/).
- Lyu C, Zhang Y, Gu M, Huang Y, Liu G, Wang C et al. (2018). IRAK-M Deficiency Exacerbates Ischemic Neurovascular Injuries in Experimental Stroke Mice. *Frontiers in cellular neuroscience*. [PMID:30622459](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30622459/).
- Nature Reviews Immunology research highlights (2002). Textpresso document AGRKB:101000000830868 combines several highlights, and its record names only one of them (Alfred J, "C. elegans - an innate choice?"), which is not the source of the sentences cited here. Not in PubMed.
- Nechama M, Kwon J, Wei S, Kyi AT, Welner RS, Ben-Dov IZ et al. (2018). The IL-33-PIN1-IRAK-M axis is critical for type 2 immunity in IL-33-induced allergic airway inflammation. *Nature communications*. [PMID:29686383](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29686383/).
- Nolan A, Kobayashi H, Naveed B, Kelly A, Hoshino Y, Hoshino S et al. (2009). Differential role for CD80 and CD86 in the regulation of the innate immune response in murine polymicrobial sepsis. *PloS one*. [PMID:19672303](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19672303/).
- Rothschild DE, Zhang Y, Diao N, Lee CK, Chen K, Caswell CC et al. (2017). Enhanced Mucosal Defense and Reduced Tumor Burden in Mice with the Compromised Negative Regulator IRAK-M. *EBioMedicine*. [PMID:27939424](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27939424/).
- Sung NY, Yang MS, Song DS, Kim JK, Park JH, Song BS et al. (2013). Procyanidin dimer B2-mediated IRAK-M induction negatively regulates TLR4 signaling in macrophages. *Biochem Biophys Res Commun*. [PMID:23872113](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23872113/).
- Wesche H, Gao X, Li X, Kirschning CJ, Stark GR, Cao Z (1999). IRAK-M is a novel member of the Pelle/interleukin-1 receptor-associated kinase (IRAK) family. *J Biol Chem*. [PMID:10383454](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10383454/).
title: PAINT issue: PTHR24419: IRAK3 (IRAK-M) inherits "positive regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction" from paralogs, although it is mainly described as an inhibitor of NF-kappaB signaling

author: goldturtle
body:
Update after checking the latest annotation data: the main argument above no longer holds.

In the UniProt-GOA human file of 2026-11-04, the gain of *positive regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction* (GO:0043123) at PTN008405164 was re-curated on 2026-08-28. It now also rests on mouse Irak1 (MGI:107420) and mouse Irak3 (MGI:1921164), IRAK3's ortholog. So the "inherited from paralogs only" argument and the suggested loss at PTN000701385 are outdated; please disregard them. Our analysis used the PAN-GO 2025-10-12 release, which predates that change.

The remaining point is not a PAN-GO one: IRAK3's only opposing experimental annotation, an IMP to *negative regulation of canonical NF-kappaB signal transduction* (GO:0043124) from PMID:10383454, seems to reverse its paper. The same 2024 curation gives this IMP to IRAK1 and IRAK2 as well. That is a question for the curators of those annotations.

Sorry for the noise. Closing.
